problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`. You may assume each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
hints: A brute force approach checks every pair — can you do better with a lookup structure?
A hash map lets you check if the complement of the current number has been seen in O(1).

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.description: Given a sorted array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, write a function that returns the index of `target` or -1 if it is not present, in O(log n) time.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order.
hints: Narrow the search space by comparing the middle element to the target each iteration.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description: Given a string containing just the characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, determine if the input string is valid — every opening bracket is closed by the same type in the correct order.
hints: A stack is a natural fit for tracking the most recent unmatched opening bracket.

problems.title: Merge Intervals
problems.description: Given an array of intervals where `intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i]`, merge all overlapping intervals and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.
hints: Sort by start time first — overlaps can then only happen between consecutive intervals.
